messages:
ACME SRE: Hey team, we're seeing repeated 502s and tail latency spikes on our Dedicated cluster for model 'redwood-7b-instruct' starting ~2026-03-15T18:12Z. Example request id: req_0a1b2c3d4e. Errors in response: "upstream read timeout" and sometimes "connection reset by peer". Can you help gather repro steps and node logs?

Maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces the issue and confirm the region + dedicated pool id? Also please include the exact request_id you saw in the error.

ACME SRE: Minimal curl we used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-instruct","input":"summarize: long document...","max_tokens":512}' \
```
Pool: dedicated-us-west-2-a, region us-west-2. Request IDs: req_0a1b2c3d4e, req_0f9e8d7c6b. Happens ~5% of requests, latency jumps from p50 ~80ms to p95 >3s and then 502.

Maya (Support): Thanks. Raj from infra is looped. Raj, can you grab pod and node logs, GPU metrics for that pool and the timeframe? If possible include k8s events and kubelet logs.

Raj (Eng-Infra): On it. Starting with kubectl lines to collect:
```bash
# list pods in pool namespace
kubectl -n dedicated-us-west-2-a get pods -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated-us-west-2-a
# describe suspicious pod
kubectl -n dedicated-us-west-2-a describe pod infer-67f4b9c
# grab recent logs
kubectl -n dedicated-us-west-2-a logs infer-67f4b9c --previous --tail=200
# node dmesg for kernel OOM / GPU errors
ssh node-23 sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200; sudo dmesg | tail -n 80; sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 80
# nvidia metrics
ssh node-23 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits"
```

Raj (Eng-Infra): Pulled outputs; summarizing top bits:
- Pod infer-67f4b9c restartCount=4 in last 2 hours.
- kubectl logs (previous) shows repeated error: "failed to allocate kv cache for sequence length 4096: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation" and then runtime exit.
- kubelet journal shows: "kubelet: Evicting pod infer-67f4b9c due to node allocatable pressure" at 18:13:04 UTC.
- dmesg shows kernel OOM killed python process pid=31245 total-vm=12000000kB RSS=11000000kB
- nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
0, GPU-1234abcd, 98, 12650, 16384, 77
1, GPU-2345bcde, 3, 512, 16384, 45
```
Interpretation: GPU 0 memory 12.6GB/16GB and almost fully utilized (98% util), GPU 1 mostly free. Pod anti-affinity placement seems to have put multiple heavy pods on same GPU.

ACME SRE: That matches what we saw — some calls hit the busy GPU and error. Our client traffic is bursty. Is there automatic fallback or placement policy we can tweak while you investigate?

Sara (Runtime): We have placement policy set to prefer single-GPU packing for small models, but large batch windows can cause hot spots. Immediate mitigation: enable inter-pod spreading or set request-level GPU preference to "balanced". Also we can configure a fast fallback to a CPU-backed replica or a smaller batch size.

Maya (Support): For repro bundle, please collect:
- full pod logs (current + previous) for involved pods
- kubelet journal excerpt around the timestamps (18:00-18:30 UTC)
- node dmesg/kern logs
- nvidia-smi continuous samples (we recommend 30s interval for 10 minutes)
- the raw request_ids and curl reproducer (you already gave two)
I can share an upload link for the debug bundle.

ACME SRE: Uploading logs now (link provided privately). Also attaching one full failed response with headers: "x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d4e", "x-internal-shard: node-23" and response body contains "upstream read timeout".

Raj (Eng-Infra): Quick check of scheduler events: I see a transient spike in pod placements at 18:11-18:14 — three new infer pods booted and were scheduled on node-23. Looks like a batch rollout overlapped with customer traffic. I opened a quick fix: cordon node-23 for scheduling of new heavy pods and draining non-critical ones.

Sara (Runtime): I'm going to push a runtime config change to reduce default batch window from 50ms -> 20ms for the pool (canary to 10% of traffic) to limit memory pressure. Patching now. Will monitor.

oncall-bot: Deploy started: runtime-config-change batch-window -> 20ms on pool dedicated-us-west-2-a (canary 10%). CI status: ✅

Raj (Eng-Infra): After cordon, node-23 GPU0 utilization dropped to ~65% and no new OOMs seen in the last 8 minutes. Pod restarts stopped. Still want full debug bundle to confirm root cause.

ACME SRE: Thanks — after your interventions error rate dropped to near 0 and latency normalized. We'll keep the bundle up for 24h. Can you confirm whether billing or dropped requests need special handling? We had several requests that returned 502s — want to make sure clients aren't billed for failed tokens.

Maya (Support): We'll run a billing check for the request_ids you provided and flag any improper charges. Also we'll follow up with a post-mortem summary and recommended config changes: prefer spreading, smaller batch windows on dedicated pools with heterogeneous GPU counts, and a scheduler constraint to avoid packing three heavy pods onto the same node.

Sara (Runtime): Action items: 1) finish canary -> roll 100% if no regressions. 2) add placement safeguard to scheduler (low-risk). 3) add an alert rule for sustained per-GPU memory >90% for >2min.

Maya (Support): Thanks all. ACME SRE — I'll follow up in 2 hours with billing check and a timeline. :thumbsup:
